data.turoyo: Laḥmo, d uxalwo, latwo. Kafno pis we, kallat lə mipayadwo. Šuġlo latwo w ʕamlo latwo.
data.translation: There was no bread to eat. Hunger was bad; they could not find so much as a little. There was no work and no labour.

summary: All four occurrences fit II.1 procurement; no new sense, form box or idiom. Two supplied passages repeat existing examples despite different citation formats. Null example sense labels in the source belong to the sole sense 1; inherited text is preserved.

Beneficiary -lan in payadlan contrasts with -la/-a in the existing examples. The prefixless Imperativ is already part of the entry, so payəd is not a new box. Permitted lookup confirms fyd II has the same etymology and gloss with f- forms; do not infer a regional distribution from these few tokens.

The fyd variant has the same Kurdish etymology, active procurement sense and an inherited Detransitive Infectum example lo ... k-mifayəd eba. It supplies direct morphological/semantic support for the new pyd Detransitive Infectum-wa proposal.
One occurrence is sufficient for this clear regular counterpart, but the pyd versus fyd distribution and native reduction require review. R1 proposed no Detransitive and is not duplicated.
The supplied project machine English loses the money noun kallat. It is retained verbatim and explicitly flagged, never used to classify the patient as food or to establish a new quantifier sense.

Align PrS 68/55 with inherited prs 194/27 and PrS 68/56 with inherited prs 103/140. Are these parallel text/page citation systems or an inherited miscitation? No fix-citation is justified by the present input alone.
